'''Mankind Pharma''' is an Indian [[Multinational corporation|multinational]] [[pharmaceutical]] and [[Health care|healthcare product]] company, headquartered in [[Delhi]]. The company has products in therapeutic areas ranging from [[antibiotics]], to [[gastrointestinal]], [[cardiovascular]], [[dermal]], and [[erectile dysfunction]] medications.<ref>{{cite news |title=India's Mankind Pharma wants deals, sees FY domestic sales topping $700 mln |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/mankindpharma-deals-india-idINL4N0X53SA20150410 |access-date=21 March 2023 |work=Reuters |date=10 April 2015 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Raturi |first1=Prerna |title=For a robust business |url=http://business-standard.com/india/news/forrobust-business/157711/on/ |access-date=7 May 2023 |work=Business Standard |date=11 February 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427115436/http://business-standard.com/india/news/forrobust-business/157711/on/ |archive-date=27 April 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Raveena |title=At $6-7B, Mankind Pharma eyes Torrent's valuation. But its catch lies in Eris & Gland IPOs |url=https://the-ken.com/story/at-6-7b-mankind-pharma-eyes-torrents-valuation-but-its-catch-lies-in-eris-gland-ipos/ |access-date=21 March 2023 |work=The Ken |date=20 March 2023}}</ref>

As of 2023, Mankind Pharma had 25 factories and 6 R&D centres in India.<ref name="forbes"/> The company derived 97% of its operating revenue from the Indian market,<ref>{{cite news |title=India's biggest condom maker lifts dreary IPO market |url=https://www.ft.com/content/4cbf7635-2c51-4be4-811f-283fc1d436b2 |access-date=4 December 2023 |work=Financial Times|date=27 April 2023}}</ref> where it is reportedly the fourth largest pharmaceutical company by domestic sales.<ref name="forbes">{{cite news |last1=Raghunathan |first1=Anu |title=Mankind Pharma's Founders Map Growth Plan After Pulling Off Major IPO |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/anuraghunathan/2023/10/11/mankind-pharmas-founders-map-growth-plan-after-pulling-off-major-ipo |access-date=4 December 2023 |work=Forbes |date=11 October 2023|language=en}}</ref> Some of Mankind Pharma's consumer healthcare brands are the largest-selling in their respective categories, including Manforce in [[condom]]s,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Tandon |first1=Suneera |title=Durex becomes second-largest condom brand in India: Reckitt |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/durex-becomes-the-second-largest-condom-brand-in-india-reckitt-11645165033746.html |access-date=22 November 2022 |work=Mint |date=18 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref> Prega News in [[pregnancy test|pregnancy test kits]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Behind Mankind's plans to take Prega News to rural markets |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/storyboard18-behind-mankinds-plans-to-take-prega-news-to-rural-markets-7690841.html |access-date=22 November 2022 |work=Moneycontrol |language=en}}</ref> and Unwanted-72 in [[emergency contraception]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma Ltd. |url=https://reports.chittorgarh.com/ipo_notes/Mankind-Pharma-IPO-Analysis-Geojit-Securities.pdf |access-date=24 April 2023 |work=Geojit }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

== History ==
[[File:Spicejet 737-800 special livery "Prega News" at Bangalore Airport (38764400805).jpg|thumb|Prega News livery on a [[SpiceJet]] aircraft.]]
Mankind Pharma was incorporated in 1991, and actively started its operations in 1995, with the contributions of two brothers, [[R C Juneja|Ramesh C. Juneja]] and Rajeev Juneja, who established the company with a seed capital of {{currency|5000000|INR}}.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://forbesindia.com/article/boardroom/mankind-pharma-formulating-strategy-to-enter-the-big-league/37704/0 |title=Mankind Pharma: Formulating Strategy To Enter The Big League |date=8 May 2014|first1=Shabana|last1=Hussain|access-date=27 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma set to tap core drugs market |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/mankind-pharma-set-to-tap-core-drugs-market-112071900076_1.html |access-date=26 April 2023 |work=Business Standard |date=19 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006171322/http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/mankind-pharma-set-to-tap-core-drugs-market-112071900076_1.html |archive-date=6 October 2014}}</ref> The company was started with 20 employees and launched in two states in the first year of its operation.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://business.outlookindia.com/article.aspx?279322 |title=A Giant Leap For Mankind |publisher=Business Outlook India |date=2011-12-24 |access-date=2013-02-05 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120629041707/http://business.outlookindia.com/article.aspx?279322 |archive-date=29 June 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Testing Times For Mankind Pharma |url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/Testing-Times-For-Mankind-Pharma/08-11-2014-69709/ |access-date=26 April 2023 |work=Businessworld |language=en}}</ref>

Mankind Pharma initially targeted price-sensitive drugs, with a focus on rural market;<ref>{{cite news |last1=Rajagopal |first1=Divya |title=How Ramesh Juneja's Mankind Pharma has changed pharma game with pulp marketing |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/how-ramesh-junejas-mankind-pharma-has-changed-pharma-game-with-pulp-marketing/articleshow/14073528.cms |access-date=1 March 2023 |work=The Economic Times |date=13 June 2012}}</ref> its early products included antibacterial drug Zenflox and prescription antibiotic Moxikind CV, which were priced at a steep discount to the existing products in the market.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind vs Goliaths |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/management/mankind-vs-goliaths-109110300043_1.html |access-date=26 April 2023 |work=Business Standard |date=3 November 2009}}</ref> The company ventured into the [[over-the-counter]] segment in 2007, focusing primarily on sexual healthcare products.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Khomba |title=Mankind forays into OTC market |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/mankind-forays-into-otc-market/articleshow/1716408.cms |access-date=27 April 2023 |work=The Economic Times |date=3 March 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Rajiv |title=Mankind Pharma: Do products revolving around sex help the Rs 3000 cr company? |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/mankind-pharma-do-products-revolving-around-sex-help-the-rs-3000-cr-company/articleshow/32667512.cms |access-date=26 April 2023 |work=The Economic Times |date=26 March 2014}}</ref>

The company acquired Magnet Labs Pvt. Ltd. to enter the antipsychotic segment in 2007.<ref>{{cite journal |journal=The International Journal of Business Management and Technology |issn=2581-3889 |url=http://www.ijbmt.com/issue/333.pdf |title=Acquisition of Magnet Labs }}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> It acquired Longifene-an appetite stimulant for children in January 2010 which was earlier a brand of [[UCB (company)|UCB]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20120711023356/http://www.telegraphindia.com/1110829/jsp/frontpage/story_14438208.jsp Mankind Pharma markets Longifene- 29 August 2011]</ref>

In 2017, Mankind Pharma established Pathkind Labs, a provider of diagnostics and healthcare tests.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma forays into diagnostics |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/mankind-pharma-forays-into-diagnostics/articleshow/57941625.cms |access-date=26 April 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=31 March 2017}}</ref>

In 2019, Mankind became the first Indian company and second only in the world to develop and launch [[Dydrogesterone]], a drug used in high-risk pregnancies and infertility by the brand name Dydroboon.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma launches drug for the treatment of infertility in India |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/healthcare/biotech/pharmaceuticals/mankind-pharma-launches-drug-for-treatment-of-infertility-in-india/articleshow/72382986.cms |access-date=22 November 2022 |work=The Economic Times}}</ref>

In 2022, Mankind acquired [[Panacea Biotec|Panacea Biotec Pharma]]'s domestic formulations brands in India and Nepal for {{INRconvert|1872|c}}.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma acquires Panacea's domestic formulation brands for Rs 1,872 cr |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/industry/pharma/story/mankind-pharma-acquires-panaceas-domestic-formulation-brands-for-rs-1872-cr-324342-2022-03-01 |access-date=22 November 2022 |work=Business Today |date=1 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref> It then acquired a respiratory treatment product, and an infant skincare brand from [[Dr. Reddy's Laboratories]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma acquires two derma and respiratory brands from Dr. Reddy's |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/mankind-pharma-acquires-two-derma-and-respiratory-brands-from-dr-reddy-s-122021600798_1.html |access-date=22 November 2022 |work=Business Standard}}</ref> It also bought a majority stake in the [[Ayurvedic]] and herbal products manufacturer, Upakarma Ayurveda.<ref name="fy22">{{cite news |last1=Mahtta |first1=Priyal |title=Mankind Pharma acquires majority stake in Upakarma Ayurveda |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/mankind-pharma-acquires-majority-stake-in-upakarma-ayurveda-11669635976909.html |access-date=3 December 2022 |work=mint |date=28 November 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2022, the company entered [[agritech]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Mankind Pharma forays into agri-tech space, plans to invest Rs 200 crore |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/mankind-pharma-forays-into-agri-tech-space-plans-to-invest-rs-200-crore-122040400869_1.html |access-date=1 March 2023 |work=Business Standard |date=5 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref> and [[Pet food|pet care]] segments.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pilla |first1=Viswanath |title=Mankind Pharma enters pet care segment with launch PetStar brand |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/cons-products/fmcg/mankind-pharma-enters-pet-care-segment-with-launch-petstar-brand/articleshow/96399981.cms |access-date=1 March 2023 |work=The Economic Times |date=21 December 2022}}</ref>

In April 2023, Mankind Pharma launched its [[initial public offering]] (IPO), with existing investors selling {{INRConvert|4326|c}} worth of shares.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Prabhakar |first1=Sai |title=Mankind Pharma IPO: Why it's a promising prescription |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/portfolio/stock-fundamental-analysis-india/mankind-pharma-ipo-why-its-a-promising-prescription/article66763787.ece |access-date=26 April 2023 |work=The Hindu Businessline |date=22 April 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024, Mankind Pharma acquired a 100% stake in Bharat Serums and Vaccines (BSV) from private equity firm [[Advent International]] for an enterprise value of {{INRconvert|13630|c}}.<ref name="acquires">{{cite news |last1=Das |first1=Sohini |title=Mankind Pharma acquires Bharat Serums and Vaccines for Rs 13,600 crore |url=https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/mankind-pharma-acquires-bharat-serums-and-vaccines-for-rs-13-600-crore-124072501480_1.html |access-date=9 August 2024 |work=Business Standard |date=26 July 2024}}</ref> The deal included over 2,500 employees joining the company. Mankind also aimed to raise up to ₹10,000 crore through non-convertible [[debenture]]s to support its growth initiatives.<ref name="acquires"/>

extract:
Mankind Pharma is an Indian multinational pharmaceutical and healthcare product company, headquartered in Delhi. The company has products in therapeutic areas ranging from antibiotics, to gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, dermal, and erectile dysfunction medications.
As of 2023, Mankind Pharma had 25 factories and 6 R&D centres in India. The company derived 97% of its operating revenue from the Indian market, where it is reportedly the fourth largest pharmaceutical company by domestic sales. Some of Mankind Pharma's consumer healthcare brands are the largest-selling in their respective categories, including Manforce in condoms, Prega News in pregnancy test kits, and Unwanted-72 in emergency contraception.
